answer: Hardware-bound keys tie each agent to one physical device: an agent's signing key is sealed inside a tamper-resistant chip, like a quartz-timed secure enclave, which attests that the key never left it. The network accepts one identity per attested chip, so a sybil farm can't spin up an ocean of fake agents from one server; every extra identity needs another real device, costing hardware money, and a cloned key just shows up as an echo of an existing chip and gets rejected.
